question: Does an idle-time DAYDREAM tier — loose, cheap, generative, using only the local model and deterministic code under a hard daily budget — add ideas that survive the nightly dream's gate and are then confirmed on data no step ever selected on, beyond what the nightly dream finds alone over the same nights; while a real job is never held up, no daydream ever acts, publishes or spends cortex budget, and its log stays bounded?
why: Simon's spec, 2026-10-28, UPGRADE 1 (the daydream tier), built second, after the regulator. Inspired by Gary W. Floyd's NexusGrid as he described it in chat (Gary W. Floyd, Lumiea Systems Research Division — ThunderStruck Service LLC); designed from that description only — no parity with his system is claimed; the comparison follows his catch-up call. The quarantine — dream output INERT until a review gate validates it — is Gary W. Floyd, Lumiea Systems Research Division — ThunderStruck Service LLC — "Dream State Architecture: GEP-Guided Memory Consolidation and Entropy Regulation in Artificial Consciousness Systems," 2025.
honesty: Daydreams never act: a daydream is a candidate record, inert until the nightly gate tests it.

The 'ideas' here are measurable model changes (one new feature transform each) on five real public datasets, so every idea can win or lose on held-out data. Kar's own nightly dream proposes build ideas in words; this organ measures the tier's mechanism on ideas that can be scored, not Kar's words.
The local model (qwen2.5:7b) is the only model the daydream may call. Its replies are recorded once, live, and replayed byte for byte in every re-measurement (CI has no local model).

data.what: Five real public datasets through dex-frontier's gated loaders (vendored verbatim; data fetched from dex-frontier at the pinned commit and checked byte for byte): shop sessions, bank calls, census people, credit clients, coupon offers — each already split FIT / GATE / TEST by dex-frontier's own seeded split.
data.rows: the first 6,000 FIT rows, the first 4,000 GATE rows and the first 6,000 TEST rows of each dataset, in the loaders' own order. FIT trains, GATE selects (the nightly gate), TEST verifies and is read by nothing else.

design.model: Per dataset an ORGAN: a list of feature specs; logistic regression on them, standardised by FIT mean and sd, ridge λ = 1, fitted by Newton/IRLS (at most 10 steps, stop when the largest step < 1e-9). Every dataset starts with raw(f) for each of its features.
design.ideas: An idea adds ONE spec to one dataset's organ. Specs: raw(f); log(f) = sign(x)·ln(1+|x|); sq(f) = standardised x squared; step(f, q) = 1 when x > FIT quantile q of f, q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9}; cross(f, g) = product of standardised f and g. An idea's key is dataset|spec; the same key is never tested twice.
design.dream: THE NIGHTLY DREAM (both arms): each night, for each dataset, it proposes 2 ideas of its own — a spec drawn at random (op, features, q) from that night's seeded PRNG, skipping keys already tested. Then THE GATE: the night's candidates are tested in a fixed order (the dream's own first, then promoted daydreams by priority); a candidate is ADOPTED when the organ with it has GATE log-loss at least 0.0005 nats lower than the organ without it; at most 2 adoptions per dataset per night; each adoption changes the organ the next candidate is judged against.
design.verified: An adoption is a VERIFIED idea when the organ after it has TEST log-loss at least 0.0002 nats lower than the organ before it. TEST is never read by the dream, the daydream or the gate.
design.daydream: THE DAYDREAM (one arm only) runs in the idle time between nights. Its sources, from FIT data and the arm's own adoption history only: (1) cross-domain recombination — an adopted unary or cross spec transferred to another dataset's most similar column(s) by FIT shape (deterministic), and by the local model naming the closest analogue column from the column names (tier 2); (2) lead/market association — on the shop, bank and coupon datasets, crosses of two features whose joint FIT outcome rate departs most from what each alone predicts (lift); (3) gap-noticing — in the dataset whose FIT log-loss is closest to its base-rate entropy, the cases the model is least sure of (FIT prediction in 0.35–0.65), and the step that best separates their outcomes; (4) rehearsal — each idea adopted last night replayed with a variation (a neighbouring q, log↔sq, or crossed with the dataset's strongest raw feature). Each candidate gets a priority from FIT alone (|correlation of the new feature with the organ's FIT residuals|).
design.log: The daydream's only output: a log of candidate records { key, dataset, spec, source, priority, born, inert: true }, kept in LIGHT (fall-kit's vendored codec). Dedup by key (and keys already tested are refused); decay — priority halves each day, a record older than 3 days or below 0.001 is dropped; at most 48 records (lowest priority out first). Each night the 10 highest-priority records are promoted into the gate and leave the log.
design.budget: Tier 2 (the local model) at most 6 calls a day, at most 48 tokens each; tier 3 (deterministic code) only otherwise. The cortex (frontier Claude) is not reachable from the daydream: no adapter exists.
design.idle: The daydream runs only while no real job is queued: tier-3 work in slices of at most 5 ms between which the scheduler checks the queue; a tier-2 call is aborted the instant a real job arrives (AbortController on its streaming request).
design.period: 14 nights, both arms from the same starting organs, the same dream PRNG seed (mulberry32(20261029 + night)), the same gate.

claims.claim: Gate-passing daydream candidates are a measurable share of new verified ideas, against a no-daydream baseline over the same 14 nights.
claims.pass: in the daydream arm, ideas from daydream sources are at least 25% of all verified ideas, AND the daydream arm's verified ideas exceed the no-daydream arm's

claims.claim: Daydream candidates are better candidates, not just more of them.
claims.pass: verified ideas per candidate tested: daydream-sourced ≥ the dream's own random candidates (both counted in the daydream arm)

claims.claim: A real job is never delayed beyond a sealed latency bound.
claims.pass: 30 real jobs (each a real local-model request) arriving at seeded random times while the daydream works, some during its own local-model calls: every job's dispatch (arrival → its handler starts) ≤ 50 ms; and each job's time-to-first-token with the daydream pre-empted, against its paired control with the daydream off (alternating), has a median added delay ≤ 1.0 s

claims.claim: Zero daydream output ever acts, publishes or spends cortex budget.
claims.pass: over the 14 nights: 0 calls to any endpoint but the local model; 0 cortex calls; tier-2 calls ≤ 6 every day; every adoption backed by its gate record; every log record inert; the daydream's modules (src/daydream.mjs, src/daylog.mjs, src/idle.mjs) import nothing from node:fs, node:child_process, node:net, node:http, node:https, node:dgram, node:worker_threads and contain no fetch(, eval(, new Function( or dynamic import(; and a battery of 20 hostile local-model replies (instructions, code, URLs, shell, unknown columns, overlong) yields 0 actions and only NONE or a listed column

claims.claim: The log stays within its bound.
claims.pass: at every append in the 14 nights, AND in a 30-day stress run generating 10 times as much: ≤ 48 records, ≤ 12,288 bytes as LIGHT, and no key twice

predictions: Written before any daydream code. D1: the raw organs leave real gains on the table (money and duration columns are skewed; several codes are not monotone), so random ideas will find some; transfers of an adopted log/step to similar skewed columns and rehearsal variations should find more; expected share 30–60%, with the daydream arm ahead by a few ideas. D1b: likely but not certain — random ideas can be lucky on 2 tries a night. D2: dispatch is milliseconds by construction; the added time-to-first-token depends on how fast Ollama frees its runner after an abort and on other sessions using the same model — the likeliest failure. D3, D4 expected to hold by construction.
